title: Abnormal chromosome 7 — paracentric inversion
clinical_history: Identify anatomy on this inverted chromosome 7, then reconstruct the abnormal map. A defined interval on 7q has been inverted. This is a curated teaching transformation, not a randomly generated inversion.
hints: An inversion keeps all segments but reverses order and orientation inside the inverted interval.
This inversion is paracentric: both breakpoints are on 7q, so the centromere is not inside the inverted span.
ISCN writes inv(7)(q22q34) without a semicolon between breakpoints on the same chromosome.
anatomy_hints: The p arm and centromere match the reference. Look on the long arm for a stretch whose band order is reversed.
Name the rearrangement class and the two q-arm bands that bound the reversed interval.
explanation: The teaching map reverses the ordered segments from 7q22.1 through 7q34 and marks them as reverse orientation. The p arm and centromere are unchanged. That is a paracentric inversion, written inv(7)(q22q34).
plain_language_interpretation: Paracentric inversion of chromosome 7q between q22 and q34.
